relations.instance_semantics: AI system uses one or more model artifacts
AI system may expose agent actors
AI agent uses prompt or agent configuration
AI incident report names affected AI systems

model.name: AI System
model.purpose: Describe a governed AI-enabled system as a unit of accountability that is larger than any single model artifact: its identity, declared purpose, composition, classification, lifecycle, operation, oversight, assurance evidence and retirement.
model.scope_statement: WM-AI-001 covers the machine-based system that infers from input how to generate outputs influencing physical or virtual environments, taken together with the provider/deployer arrangements, configuration baseline, human oversight, logging, evaluation evidence and regulatory status that make it operable and auditable. It is format-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of the same semantics. It stops at the boundary of the model artifact, the agent actor, the dataset and the incident report, which are separately modelled and linked by typed edges.
in_scope: Authoritative system identity, trade name, identification reference and public registration identifiers
Declared intended purpose, conditions of use, excluded uses and reasonably foreseeable misuse
Autonomy and adaptiveness profile, output types and the environments outputs can influence
Regulatory and internal risk classification, including derogation claims and profiling flags
Versioned configuration baseline and the component set frozen in it (AI bill of materials)
Binding to model artifacts, upstream providers and external model services
Input data dependencies, input specifications and deployer-controlled input governance
Operator roles: provider, deployer, importer, distributor, authorised representative and internal AI actor functions
Lifecycle stage, market status, change control and substantial-modification determination
Deployment topology, processing locations, integration interfaces and market jurisdictions
Automatic event logging, runtime operational state and containment triggers
Human oversight measures, assignment, competence and intervention mechanisms
Performance metrics, declared accuracy, validation and testing evidence
Cybersecurity controls and adversarial threat posture
Conformity assessment, declarations, standards applied and public registration records
Transparency disclosure to affected persons and machine-readable marking of synthetic output
Risk management system and impact assessment on persons and fundamental rights
Post-market monitoring, serious incident detection and reporting linkage
Retention, decommissioning, withdrawal and deletion
out_of_scope: Internal structure, weights, architecture, training run and evaluation of the model artifact itself (WM-SFT-004)
Agent actor goals, tool repertoire, planning loops and autonomous task execution semantics (WM-AI-002)
The AI incident report record and its regulatory narrative content (WM-AI-010)
Dataset content, dataset licensing and dataset lineage as first-class records
Legal entity, organisational structure and personnel records of the provider or deployer
Generic software product packaging, release engineering and non-AI functionality inherited from WM-SFT-002
Data subject, natural person and consent records
Enterprise risk register, audit programme and management-system certification scope of the organisation
Hardware/device product records where the AI system is only an embedded safety component
Contract, procurement and commercial terms records

boundary_notes.distinction: The model artifact is a versioned trained object with parameters and a training provenance chain. WM-AI-001 records only the binding: which artifact version is invoked, in which role, under which access mode. Regulators separate the two regimes explicitly, treating general-purpose models and AI systems as distinct objects of obligation.

An AI system may expose zero, one or many agent actors. Agent-specific semantics (goal decomposition, tool invocation, memory, delegation) belong to WM-AI-002; WM-AI-001 records only that agent actors exist, their autonomy envelope and the containment controls around them.

WM-AI-001 owns detection, classification and the reporting obligation state for the system; the incident report record itself, with its narrative, causal analysis and authority correspondence, is a separate record that names the affected AI system.

WM-AI-001 specialises the software parent with the elements that only apply when a system infers outputs rather than executing fully specified rules: inference-derived behaviour, adaptiveness after deployment and autonomy. Deterministic rule engines without an inference step are out of scope even when embedded in the same product.

WM-AI-001 records the input data specification and the identifiers of datasets relied upon, not the dataset contents, collection method or labelling procedure, which are documented in the model artifact and dataset models.

Certificates are issued to a version of a system by an external body and have their own identity and expiry. WM-AI-001 holds the reference and status, not the certificate lifecycle of the issuing body.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Medical device or other sectoral product record
boundary_notes.distinction: Where the AI system is a device software function, sectoral lifecycle regimes add pre-authorised change control constructs that are not present in the horizontal regime; WM-AI-001 carries a change-plan reference rather than duplicating sectoral device documentation.

sources.title: Article 3: Definitions — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of AI system, provider, deployer, intended purpose, substantial modification, serious incident and general-purpose AI model that set the model boundary.

sources.title: Annex IV: Technical Documentation referred to in Article 11(1) — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Enumerates the required documentation items for a high-risk AI system: general description, development, monitoring and control, metrics, risk management, lifecycle changes, standards, declaration and post-market plan.

sources.title: Annex VIII: Information to be submitted upon registration of high-risk AI systems — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Annex VIII Sections A, B, C
sources.relevance: Defines the public registration data set for provider and deployer, including trade name, identification reference, status, certificate data and impact assessment summaries.

sources.title: Article 12: Record-keeping — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Requires automatic event logging over the lifetime of the system and specifies minimum log content for remote biometric identification, including start and end date and time of each use.

sources.title: Article 26: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Deployer duties: use per instructions, assign competent human oversight, ensure input data relevance and representativeness, monitor, retain logs at least six months, inform workers and affected persons.

sources.title: Article 73: Reporting of serious incidents — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Sets awareness-triggered reporting deadlines (15 days general, 2 days for widespread infringement or critical infrastructure disruption, 10 days for death) and the subsequent investigation duty.

sources.title: Article 6: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Two classification routes (product safety and listed use case), the four derogation conditions, the profiling exception and the duty to document a non-high-risk assessment before placing on the market.

sources.title: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Requires disclosure of AI interaction, machine-readable marking of synthetic audio, image, video and text, deep fake disclosure and notification for emotion recognition and biometric categorisation.

sources.title: Article 72: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan — AI Act
sources.organization: European Commission — AI Act Service Desk
sources.relevance: Requires a proportionate post-market monitoring system, systematic collection of performance data over the lifetime including data from deployers, and inclusion of the plan in the technical documentation.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Voluntary framework structured as GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE and MANAGE covering design, development, use and evaluation of AI products, services and systems across the lifecycle.

sources.title: AI Risks and Trustworthiness — NIST AI RMF section 3
sources.relevance: Defines the seven trustworthiness characteristics — valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, fair with harmful bias managed — used as evaluation dimensions.

sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations, NIST AI 100-2 E2025
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Attack taxonomy (evasion, poisoning, privacy, abuse/misuse) tied to lifecycle stages of attack and to attacker goals, capabilities and knowledge; grounds the AI-specific threat model.

sources.title: What is AI? Can you make a clear distinction between AI and non-AI systems?
sources.version_or_date: Updated OECD AI system definition, adopted November 2023
sources.relevance: Element-by-element reading of machine-based, explicit or implicit objectives, inference, output types, influence on physical or virtual environments, and varying autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment.

sources.title: Explanatory memorandum on the updated OECD definition of an AI system (OECD Artificial Intelligence Papers No. 8)
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.relevance: Authoritative rationale for each definitional element and for the lifecycle framing that separates design and development from deployment, operation and monitoring.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent model with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, startedAtTime and endedAtTime; the alignment target for system provenance and change history.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar requiring four-digit years, seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z, with -00:00 reserved for an unknown local offset.

sources.title: ECMA-424: CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification
sources.relevance: Standardised inventory format for components, services, dependencies, vulnerabilities and machine learning models; the interoperability target for the system component inventory.

sources.title: CycloneDX Machine Learning Bill of Materials (ML-BOM / AI-BOM)
sources.relevance: Describes documenting datasets, models and configurations for AI systems to support bias, data integrity and model security risk assessment across the AI supply chain.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Management system
sources.relevance: Management-system requirements (clauses 4-10) and Annex A controls covering AI policy, impact assessment, lifecycle, data management, third-party relationships and operational monitoring; used only as an alignment, not a conformance claim.

sources.title: Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions
sources.relevance: Non-EU counterexample for change governance: a pre-authorised plan of Description of Modifications, Modification Protocol and Impact Assessment lets a system evolve without a new submission.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council (Artificial Intelligence Act), consolidated
sources.relevance: Binding definitions of AI system, provider, deployer and related operators; intended purpose; substantial modification; high-risk requirements including technical documentation, logging, human oversight, post-market monitoring, documentation keeping, registration, recall and withdrawal.

sources.title: OECD Framework for the Classification of AI systems
sources.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.relevance: Policy classification dimensions People and Planet, Economic Context, Data and Input, AI Model, and Task and Output, used to characterise a deployed AI system without collapsing it to a model.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Voluntary lifecycle risk management for organisations designing, developing, deploying or using AI systems; Govern-Map-Measure-Manage functions; trustworthiness characteristics; AI actors across the lifecycle.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology
sources.relevance: Foundational terminology for AI system, AI agent, model, lifecycle stages from inception to retirement including continuous validation and re-evaluation, and the engineered-system view of AI.

sources.title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
sources.version_or_date: CETS No. 225; EU OJ L 2026/1081 of 13.5.2026; opened for signature 2024-09-05
sources.relevance: Binding treaty definition of an artificial intelligence system aligned to the OECD text, covering lifecycle activities with potential to interfere with human rights, democracy and the rule of law, and excluding national defence.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 Information technology — Artificial intelligence (AI) — AI system impact assessment
sources.relevance: Guidance for performing and documenting AI system impact assessments on individuals and societies across lifecycle stages, integrable with AI risk management and an AI management system.

bundles.name: Identity, Purpose and Classification
bundles.description: What this AI system is, which version of it is in force, what it is declared to do, and how it is classified for risk and behaviour.
bundles.rationale: Nothing downstream is decidable until the system is uniquely identified, its intended purpose is fixed and its regulatory class is settled; both the horizontal regulation and the OECD definition make purpose, inference, autonomy and adaptiveness the discriminating attributes.

layers.name: System Identity and Versioning
layers.description: Authoritative and public identifiers for the system and the versioned configuration baseline they resolve to.

findings.name: AI system identity and designation
findings.description: The identifier set that pins one AI system as an accountable object: the master-system key, the commercial trade name, the provider's internal identification reference and any public registry entry identifiers.

questions.text: Which identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier for this AI system, and which system of record issues it?
What trade name and identification reference distinguish this system from other systems supplied by the same provider?
How is the system-level identity kept distinct from the identities of the model artifacts it invokes and the product it is embedded in?
Which external registries hold an identifier for this system, and how are those identifiers reconciled with the master key?

data_elements.name: System master identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier issued by the authoritative system of record for the AI system.

data_elements.name: Trade name
data_elements.description: Commercial name under which the system is placed on the market or put into service.

data_elements.name: Provider identification reference
data_elements.description: Unambiguous reference used by the provider to identify the system in documentation and registration.

data_elements.name: External registry entry
data_elements.description: Reference to a public or sectoral registry entry representing this system.

artifacts.name: System identity record
artifacts.description: Canonical record binding master identifier, trade names, provider references and external registry entries, independent of storage format.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the provider's system of record; a governed public registration entry identifier is carried as an alias, never as the primary key.

findings.name: Version and configuration baseline
findings.description: The released, frozen combination of software, firmware, model versions, prompts and policies that constitutes 'this system as placed on the market', together with its integrity evidence and effective dates.

questions.text: Which version and configuration baseline of the system is currently placed on the market or put into service?
Which component versions — model, software, firmware, prompts, policies — are frozen in this baseline?
How is the integrity of the released baseline demonstrated, and by which build or signing provenance?
When did this baseline take effect and when did it supersede the previous baseline?

data_elements.name: System version
data_elements.description: Version label of the AI system as a whole, distinct from any component version.

data_elements.name: Baseline component set
data_elements.description: Enumerated component identifiers and versions frozen in the baseline.

data_elements.name: Baseline integrity digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest or attestation covering the baseline manifest.

data_elements.name: Baseline effective-from
data_elements.description: Time from which the baseline is the operative configuration.

artifacts.name: Configuration baseline manifest
artifacts.description: Immutable manifest enumerating every component version, prompt, policy and firmware level in a released baseline, with integrity values.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master system identifier plus system version label; a content digest of the canonical manifest is the tie-breaker when a version is re-issued.

layers.name: Intended Purpose and Operating Domain
layers.description: The declared purpose, conditions of use, exclusions and foreseeable misuse that bound every later assessment.

findings.name: Intended purpose and operating domain
findings.description: The provider's declared use, including specific context and conditions of use, the intended user groups and environments, and the excluded uses and reasonably foreseeable misuses against which risk is assessed.

questions.text: What is the intended purpose declared by the provider, including the specific context and conditions of use?
Which uses are explicitly excluded, and which reasonably foreseeable misuses have been identified?
Which sectors, environments and affected populations does the declared purpose reach?
Who may change the declared intended purpose, and what re-assessment does such a change trigger?

data_elements.name: Intended purpose statement
data_elements.description: Provider's declaration of the use for which the system is intended, with context and conditions.

data_elements.name: Excluded use
data_elements.description: A use the provider states the system must not be put to.

data_elements.name: Reasonably foreseeable misuse
data_elements.description: An identified misuse that risk management and instructions for use must address.

data_elements.name: Intended user group
data_elements.description: Category of deployer or end user for whom the system and its interface are designed.

artifacts.name: Instructions for use
artifacts.description: Deployer-facing instructions covering intended purpose, conditions of use, interface description, limitations and required oversight measures.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus system version plus document revision; electronic instructions carry a resolvable location for registration purposes.

layers.name: Risk and Behavioural Classification
layers.description: How the system is classified for regulatory risk and how its inference behaviour, autonomy and adaptiveness are characterised.

findings.name: Regulatory and risk classification
findings.description: The determination of which regime applies — prohibited practice, high-risk by product-safety route, high-risk by listed use case, transparency-only, or minimal — including any derogation claim and the profiling exception that defeats it.

questions.text: Under which classification route does the system fall, and which listed use case or harmonisation instrument triggers it?
If a derogation from high-risk classification is claimed, which condition is relied on and what evidence supports it?
Does the system perform profiling of natural persons, which removes any derogation?
Which events require the classification to be reassessed before the system continues in service?

data_elements.name: Risk class code
data_elements.description: Coded regulatory risk classification assigned to the system.

data_elements.name: Classification route
data_elements.description: Which route produced the classification: embedded product safety component, listed use case, transparency-only or minimal.

data_elements.name: Derogation condition
data_elements.description: The narrow-procedural-task, prior-human-work, pattern-detection or preparatory-task condition relied on.

data_elements.name: Profiling flag
data_elements.description: Whether the system performs profiling of natural persons.

data_elements.name: Classification assessment time
data_elements.description: Time at which the classification determination was made.

artifacts.name: Classification assessment record
artifacts.description: Documented assessment of classification and any non-high-risk determination, prepared before placing on the market and retained for authorities.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus assessment sequence number; superseded assessments are retained rather than overwritten.

findings.name: Autonomy and adaptiveness profile
findings.description: Characterisation of how much the system decides without a human decision point, whether it changes its own behaviour after deployment, what output types it produces and which physical or virtual environments those outputs can influence.

questions.text: What level of autonomy does the system exercise between human decision points, and where are those points placed?
Does the system adapt after deployment, and through which mechanism — online learning, retrieval updates, or prompt and policy changes?
How is the boundary drawn between inference-derived behaviour and deterministic rule execution inside this system?
Which physical or virtual environments can the system's outputs influence, and through which actuators or downstream integrations?

data_elements.name: Autonomy level
data_elements.description: Coded degree of independent operation between human decision points.

data_elements.name: Adaptiveness mode
data_elements.description: How, if at all, system behaviour changes after deployment.

data_elements.name: Output type
data_elements.description: Kind of output generated: prediction, content, recommendation or decision.

data_elements.name: Environment influence scope
data_elements.description: Description of the physical or virtual environment affected by outputs and the mediating integration.

artifacts.name: System behaviour profile
artifacts.description: Record characterising inference boundary, autonomy level, adaptiveness mechanism, output types and environmental reach; the basis for deciding whether the object is in scope for AI-specific governance at all.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus system version; re-derived whenever the baseline changes an inference or actuation path.

findings.name: AI system definition
findings.description: An AI system is a machine-based or engineered system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. OECD, the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe Framework Convention share this inference-centred wording; ISO/IEC 22989 uses engineered system and human-defined objectives without the verb infers.

questions.text: Which definition of AI system is adopted for this instance and how is it distinguished from ordinary rule-executing software?
Does this instance infer how to generate predictions, content, recommendations or decisions from inputs in a way that can influence physical or virtual environments?
Which definitional conflicts between OECD, EU, ISO/IEC 22989 and NIST AI RMF 1.0 are recorded for this instance rather than claimed as conformance?

data_elements.name: Adopted definition text
data_elements.description: The definition text used to admit this record as an AI system.

data_elements.name: Definition alignment codes
data_elements.description: Instruments this instance is aligned to, such as OECD-2023, EU-2024-1689 Art 3(1), ISO-22989-3.1.4, CoE-CETS-225 Art 2, NIST-AI-RMF-1.0.

data_elements.name: Output types
data_elements.description: Whether the system produces predictions, content, recommendations, decisions or other declared outputs.

data_elements.name: Environment influence
data_elements.description: Whether outputs can influence physical environments, virtual environments, or both.

artifacts.name: Definition alignment note
artifacts.description: Record of the adopted definition, aligned instruments and unresolved wording conflicts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier of the AI system plus definition-note revision

findings.name: OECD classification dimensions
findings.description: The OECD framework classifies AI systems along People and Planet, Economic Context, Data and Input, AI Model, and Task and Output. NIST AI RMF 1.0 reuses these socio-technical dimensions to map lifecycle risk. The profile characterises a deployment; it is not itself a legal risk class.

questions.text: Who uses the system, who is impacted, and what human-rights, wellbeing, labour or environmental effects are in scope?
In which industrial sector, business function and technical-maturity setting is the system deployed?
What tasks does the system perform, does it combine tasks into a composite or autonomous control system, and what action does it take on the environment?
Does this socio-technical profile justify treating the system as in-scope for heightened governance even if no high-risk legal class applies?

data_elements.name: Impacted stakeholders
data_elements.description: Individuals and groups who interact with or are affected by the applied AI system.

data_elements.name: Industrial sector
data_elements.description: Sector of deployment such as finance, health, public administration or agriculture.

data_elements.name: System tasks
data_elements.description: Tasks performed, such as recognition, event detection, forecasting, content generation or control.

data_elements.name: Human rights and wellbeing effects
data_elements.description: Documented potential effects on human rights, wellbeing, society and the world of work.

artifacts.name: Socio-technical classification profile
artifacts.description: Completed OECD-style profile of people, economic context, data, model and task for this deployment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus profile revision

findings.name: General-purpose AI system boundary
findings.description: A general-purpose AI system is an AI system based on a general-purpose AI model and capable of serving a variety of purposes, for direct use or for integration in other AI systems. The GPAI model itself is not this entity. Downstream providers integrate a model into their AI system.

questions.text: Is this record a general-purpose AI system, a single-purpose system, or a downstream system that integrates a GPAI model?
Which general-purpose or other models are integrated, and is integration vertical or contractual with another entity?
Is any integrated model still in research, development or prototyping before being placed on the market, and therefore outside GPAI-model placing rules?

data_elements.name: GPAI system flag
data_elements.description: Whether the AI system is based on a GPAI model and can serve a variety of purposes.

data_elements.name: Downstream provider flag
data_elements.description: Whether this system's provider integrates an AI model supplied by another entity or by itself.

data_elements.name: Integrated GPAI model references
data_elements.description: References to general-purpose or other models composed into this system.

artifacts.name: GPAI system-model boundary note
artifacts.description: Statement of system generality and linked model artifacts, without storing model internals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus boundary-note revision

bundles.name: Composition and Supply Chain
bundles.description: What the system is made of, which models and data it depends on, and which parties are accountable for each part.
bundles.rationale: Technical documentation and registration both require the constituent parts and the responsible operators to be enumerable; supply-chain transparency formats exist precisely to make this inventory machine-readable.

layers.name: System Composition and Dependencies
layers.description: Component inventory, model artifact bindings and the input data the system consumes in operation.

findings.name: Component inventory and AI bill of materials
findings.description: The enumerated set of models, libraries, services, hardware and data stores that constitute the system in a given baseline, with supplier, version, licence and vulnerability status, expressed in a machine-readable bill-of-materials format.

questions.text: Which components constitute the system in the released baseline, and which are third-party rather than self-developed?
For each component, what is its supplier, licence and origin of supply?
In which machine-readable bill-of-materials format and specification version is the inventory published?
Which components carry known vulnerabilities or an unsupported end-of-life status at the time of release?

data_elements.name: Component entry
data_elements.description: One inventoried constituent of the system with type, version and supply origin.

data_elements.name: Component licence
data_elements.description: Licence under which a component is used or redistributed.

data_elements.name: BOM format identifier
data_elements.description: Name and version of the bill-of-materials specification used.

data_elements.name: Component vulnerability reference
data_elements.description: Known vulnerability affecting an inventoried component.

artifacts.name: AI bill of materials
artifacts.description: Machine-readable inventory of components, services, datasets, models and configurations with dependency relationships and vulnerability data.
artifacts.identity_strategy: BOM serial number plus BOM version, bound to the system master identifier and baseline manifest digest.

findings.name: Model artifact binding
findings.description: Which model artifacts and versions the system invokes, in which functional role, under which access mode and commercial terms, and how upstream model changes reach the system.

questions.text: Which model artifacts and versions does the system invoke, and in which role — primary, fallback, guardrail or embedding?
Is each model artifact self-developed, obtained from an upstream provider, or consumed as an external hosted service?
What licence or contractual terms govern use, modification and redistribution of each bound model artifact?
How are upstream model changes detected and propagated into the system baseline?

data_elements.name: Model artifact reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a model artifact record and version invoked by the system.

data_elements.name: Model functional role
data_elements.description: Role the bound model plays within the system pipeline.

data_elements.name: Model access mode
data_elements.description: Whether the model is embedded, hosted internally or consumed as an external service.

data_elements.name: Upstream provider identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the entity that supplied the model to the downstream provider.

artifacts.name: Model binding register
artifacts.description: Register of every model artifact version bound into a system baseline with role, access mode, supplier and change-notification channel.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus baseline identifier; each row keyed by model artifact identifier and version.

findings.name: Input data dependencies and governance
findings.description: The data streams the system consumes in operation, who controls them, the input specifications published to deployers, and the representativeness and personal-data properties that determine whether operation stays within the declared purpose.

questions.text: Which input data streams does the system consume in operation, and which party controls each stream?
How is input data shown to be relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose?
Which input fields contain personal or special-category data, and what lawful basis and safeguards apply?
What input data specifications are published to deployers so that operation remains inside the validated envelope?

data_elements.name: Input stream descriptor
data_elements.description: Description of one operational input stream including format, source and cadence.

data_elements.name: Input controller role
data_elements.description: Which operator role controls the input data for a stream.

data_elements.name: Input data specification
data_elements.description: Stated specification of input data expected by the system.

data_elements.name: Personal data category
data_elements.description: Category of personal or special-category data present in inputs.

artifacts.name: Input data specification sheet
artifacts.description: Deployer-facing description of required input data, its representativeness expectations and personal-data handling constraints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus system version plus sheet revision.

layers.name: Actors, Roles and Accountability
layers.description: Which legal entities and internal functions hold which duties for this system, and when a role changes hands.

findings.name: Operator roles and responsibility assignment
findings.description: Assignment of provider, deployer, importer, distributor and authorised representative roles to legal entities, mapped onto the internal functions that design, develop, test, deploy, operate, oversee and govern the system, plus the conditions under which a deployer becomes a provider.

questions.text: Which legal entity holds each operator role for this system in each market where it is supplied?
Which named role is accountable for placing the system on the market and for keeping technical documentation current?
Which internal functions — design, development, test and evaluation, deployment, operation, human oversight, governance — are staffed for this system?
Under which conditions does a deployer or distributor assume provider obligations for this system?

data_elements.name: Provider entity identifier
data_elements.description: Legal entity that develops or places the system on the market under its own name or trademark.

data_elements.name: Deployer entity identifier
data_elements.description: Legal entity using the system under its own authority in a professional capacity.

data_elements.name: Authorised representative
data_elements.description: Representative appointed where the provider is established outside the market jurisdiction.

data_elements.name: Role transfer trigger
data_elements.description: Recorded condition that moves provider obligations to another operator.

artifacts.name: Accountability assignment matrix
artifacts.description: Matrix binding operator roles and internal AI actor functions to entities, offices and named accountable persons, with effective periods.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus effective-period start; historical versions retained for audit rather than overwritten.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Change and Deployment
bundles.description: Where the system is in its life, how change to it is authorised, and where it actually runs.
bundles.rationale: Both the horizontal regulation and sectoral device regimes make the lifecycle change record a documentation requirement, and the OECD framing treats deployment and operation as distinct phases from design and development.

layers.name: Lifecycle State and Change Control
layers.description: Lifecycle stage, market status and the governance of modifications including pre-authorised change plans.

findings.name: Lifecycle state and transitions
findings.description: The current lifecycle stage and market status of the system, the history of transitions between them, who authorised each transition, and the gate criteria that must be met before advancing.

questions.text: Which lifecycle stage is the system in — design and development, data handling, verification and validation, deployment, or operation and monitoring?
What is the current market or service status: on the market, in service, no longer placed on the market, recalled, or withdrawn?
Who authorised each recorded state transition, and on what evidence?
Which gate criteria must be satisfied before the system may move to the next stage?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle stage code
data_elements.description: Coded lifecycle stage of the system.

data_elements.name: Market status code
data_elements.description: Coded market or service availability status.

data_elements.name: State transition event
data_elements.description: Recorded transition with prior state, new state, authoriser and time.

data_elements.name: Stage gate criterion
data_elements.description: Condition required before advancing to the next lifecycle stage.

artifacts.name: Lifecycle state log
artifacts.description: Append-only record of lifecycle and market-status transitions with authorising agent, evidence reference and both event and record times.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus monotonically increasing transition sequence number; entries are never mutated.

findings.name: Change control and substantial modification
findings.description: The determination of whether a proposed change is a substantial modification requiring renewed conformity assessment, the pre-authorised change envelope where one exists, and the impact assessment and test evidence that gate each release.

questions.text: Does the proposed change constitute a substantial modification that was not foreseen in the initial conformity assessment?
Which changes are covered by a pre-authorised change plan, and under which modification protocol are they executed?
What impact assessment supports the change, and which tests must pass before the new baseline is released?
What sequence of planned changes over the system lifetime is recorded in the technical documentation?

data_elements.name: Change request identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a proposed or executed change to the system.

data_elements.name: Change classification
data_elements.description: Whether the change is routine, pre-authorised or substantial.

data_elements.name: Modification protocol reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the protocol governing execution and verification of a pre-authorised change.

data_elements.name: Planned change schedule
data_elements.description: Documented sequence of foreseen changes over the system lifetime.

artifacts.name: Change control plan
artifacts.description: Plan describing the modifications foreseen, the protocol used to implement and verify them and the assessment of their impact on safety, performance and compliance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus plan revision identifier; each authorised revision is retained with its approval time.

layers.name: Deployment Topology and Jurisdiction
layers.description: Where and on what the system runs, what it integrates with, and which legal regimes apply in each market.

findings.name: Deployment environment and jurisdictional placement
findings.description: The environments and locations in which the system is deployed and processing occurs, the hardware and runtime resources it requires, the interfaces through which it interacts with other software, hardware and AI systems, and the jurisdictions where it is placed on the market or put into service.

questions.text: In which environments and physical or cloud locations is the system deployed, and where is inference processing actually performed?
Which hardware and computational resources does the system require to operate as intended?
Through which interfaces does the system interact with other software, hardware or AI systems that are not part of it?
In which jurisdictions is the system placed on the market or put into service, and which regulatory regime governs each?

data_elements.name: Deployment environment
data_elements.description: Named environment in which a system instance runs.

data_elements.name: Processing location
data_elements.description: Geographic or regional location where inference and data processing occur.

data_elements.name: Hardware requirement
data_elements.description: Hardware on which the system is intended to run.

data_elements.name: Market jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction in which the system is made available.

data_elements.name: Integration interface
data_elements.description: Interface through which the system exchanges data with external hardware, software or AI systems.

artifacts.name: Deployment topology description
artifacts.description: Description of environments, instances, hardware, processing locations, integration interfaces and jurisdictional placement for a system baseline.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus baseline identifier plus environment name.

bundles.name: Operation, Oversight and Assurance
bundles.description: How the system behaves in service, how humans keep control of it, how well it performs and how resilient it is to attack.
bundles.rationale: Logging, human oversight, accuracy and cybersecurity are the operative technical requirements in the horizontal regime, and the trustworthiness characteristics and adversarial taxonomy give them measurable structure.

layers.name: Runtime Operation and Logging
layers.description: Automatic event recording over the system lifetime and the live operational state of deployed instances.

findings.name: Automatic event logging capability
findings.description: The technical capability to record events automatically over the lifetime of the system at a granularity sufficient to identify risk situations, support post-market monitoring and enable deployer-side operational monitoring, with distinct event and record times and protected integrity.

questions.text: Which events does the system automatically record over its lifetime, and at what granularity?
How are event time and record or ingestion time captured and distinguished in each log entry?
Who may read operational logs, under which controls, and for which purposes?
How is log integrity protected against alteration or deletion during the retention period?

data_elements.name: Log event type
data_elements.description: Coded class of automatically recorded event.

data_elements.name: Log event time
data_elements.description: Time at which the recorded occurrence took place, including start and end times for a period of use.

data_elements.name: Log record time
data_elements.description: Time at which the event was written or ingested by the logging store.

data_elements.name: Log subject reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the input data, reference database or verifying persons associated with the event, where the use case requires it.

data_elements.name: Log integrity control
data_elements.description: Mechanism protecting log entries from undetected alteration.

artifacts.name: Operational event log
artifacts.description: Automatically generated log stream covering periods of use, inputs, decisions and verification actions over the lifetime of the system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System instance identifier plus log stream identifier plus monotonic sequence number; entries carry both event and record timestamps.

findings.name: Runtime operational state
findings.description: The live state of each deployed instance, the indicators observed continuously, and the conditions that trigger automatic containment, fallback or shutdown.

questions.text: What is the current operational state of each deployed instance — active, degraded, suspended or offline?
Which runtime indicators are observed continuously to detect deviation from validated behaviour?
Which runtime conditions trigger automatic containment, fallback or shutdown of the system?

data_elements.name: System instance identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a running deployment of the system baseline.

data_elements.name: Operational state
data_elements.description: Coded live state of an instance.

data_elements.name: Runtime indicator observation
data_elements.description: Observed value of a monitored runtime indicator with its observation time.

data_elements.name: Containment trigger
data_elements.description: Defined condition that causes automatic suspension, fallback or shutdown.

artifacts.name: Runtime status snapshot
artifacts.description: Point-in-time record of instance states and indicator observations used for operational monitoring and post-market analysis.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Instance identifier plus observation timestamp; snapshots are immutable observations, not mutable status fields.

layers.name: Human Oversight and Intervention
layers.description: Built-in and deployer-implemented oversight measures, the persons assigned to them and the mechanisms by which they intervene.

findings.name: Human oversight measures and intervention controls
findings.description: The oversight measures designed into the system, those that must be implemented by the deployer, the persons assigned with the necessary competence, training, authority and support, and the mechanisms by which they can interrupt, override or reverse system behaviour.

questions.text: Which oversight measures are built into the system by the provider and which must be implemented by the deployer?
Which natural persons are assigned oversight duties, and what competence, training and authority do they hold?
How can an overseer interrupt, override or reverse a system output, and within what time window?
How is automation bias in overseers detected and mitigated for this system?

data_elements.name: Oversight measure
data_elements.description: A specific human oversight measure applicable to the system.

data_elements.name: Oversight assignee role
data_elements.description: Role assigned to exercise human oversight in operation.

data_elements.name: Intervention mechanism
data_elements.description: Technical means by which a human halts, overrides or reverses system behaviour.

data_elements.name: Oversight competence evidence
data_elements.description: Evidence that assigned overseers have the necessary competence and training.

artifacts.name: Human oversight plan
artifacts.description: Plan describing designed-in and deployer-implemented oversight measures, assignments, intervention mechanisms and competence requirements.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus deployment context plus plan revision; deployer-specific instances reference the provider plan revision they implement.

layers.name: Performance Measurement and Evaluation
layers.description: Declared metrics and the test and validation evidence that substantiates them.

findings.name: Performance metrics and declared accuracy
findings.description: The metrics chosen to express accuracy, robustness and fairness for the intended purpose, the justification of their appropriateness, the levels declared to deployers and the conditions and degradation modes under which those levels hold.

questions.text: Which metrics express accuracy, robustness and fairness for this intended purpose, and why are they appropriate?
What levels of accuracy and robustness are declared to deployers, and under which conditions do they hold?
What are the known limitations, degradation conditions and reasonably foreseeable unintended outcomes?
How often are metrics recomputed in operation, and against which reference period and dataset?

data_elements.name: Metric definition
data_elements.description: Definition of a performance, robustness or fairness metric used for the system.

data_elements.name: Declared metric value
data_elements.description: Value of a metric declared in instructions for use or documentation.

data_elements.name: Metric applicability condition
data_elements.description: Condition under which a declared metric value is valid.

data_elements.name: Degradation condition
data_elements.description: Circumstance in which performance is known to degrade.

artifacts.name: Performance metric statement
artifacts.description: Declared metric set with values, conditions, subgroup breakdowns and limitations for a given system version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus system version plus statement revision; each value carries its observation timestamp.

findings.name: Test, validation and evaluation evidence
findings.description: The executed validation and testing procedures, the datasets used, the retained test logs and reports dated and countersigned by responsible persons, and the disposition of results that failed acceptance criteria.

questions.text: Which validation and testing procedures were executed, on which datasets, and with what results?
Which test logs and reports are retained, dated and countersigned by the responsible persons?
How are evaluation datasets shown to be separated from training data and fit for the evaluation claim made?
Which evaluation results failed acceptance criteria, and how were those failures dispositioned before release?

data_elements.name: Evaluation run identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one executed evaluation activity.

data_elements.name: Evaluation dataset reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dataset and version used in an evaluation run.

data_elements.name: Acceptance criterion
data_elements.description: Threshold or condition an evaluation result must satisfy for release.

data_elements.name: Evaluation sign-off
data_elements.description: Countersignature by the responsible person with role and time.

artifacts.name: Evaluation report
artifacts.description: Dated test and validation report with procedures, datasets, results, acceptance decisions and responsible-person sign-off.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Evaluation run identifier issued by the evaluation system of record, bound to system master identifier and system version.

layers.name: Security and Adversarial Resilience
layers.description: Protective controls and the AI-specific threat posture of the system.

findings.name: Security controls and adversarial threat posture
findings.description: The cybersecurity measures protecting the system and the explicit mapping of its exposure to adversarial attack classes — evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse — with the resilience test results and the detection and response path for AI-specific security events.

questions.text: Which cybersecurity measures protect the system against unauthorised access, model theft and infrastructure compromise?
Which adversarial attack classes are in the threat model for this system, and which residual exposures are accepted?
How is resilience against each in-scope attack class tested, and with what measured result?
What is the detection and response path for a security event that alters AI-specific behaviour rather than infrastructure?

data_elements.name: Security control
data_elements.description: Implemented technical or organisational control protecting the system.

data_elements.name: Threat class mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping of the system to an adversarial machine learning attack class and lifecycle stage of attack.

data_elements.name: Resilience test result
data_elements.description: Measured outcome of an adversarial resilience test.

data_elements.name: Security event response path
data_elements.description: Defined escalation and containment path for AI-specific security events.

artifacts.name: AI threat model and security dossier
artifacts.description: Dossier recording the threat model, control set, adversarial test results and residual risk acceptance for a system baseline.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus baseline identifier plus dossier revision; superseded revisions retained for audit.

bundles.name: Governance, Conformity and Transparency
bundles.description: The assurance case, the public record and what affected people are told.
bundles.rationale: Conformity evidence, public registration and transparency to affected persons are distinct obligations with distinct data sets, and the management-system standard places impact assessment and risk management alongside them.

layers.name: Conformity and Public Registration
layers.description: Assessment route, declarations, standards applied and the public registry record.

findings.name: Conformity assessment and declaration
findings.description: The assessment procedure followed, any notified body involved, the certificate and its expiry, the harmonised standards or common specifications applied, the justification where alternatives were adopted, and the declaration of conformity issued for a specific version.

questions.text: Which conformity assessment procedure was followed, and was a notified body involved?
Which declaration of conformity and marking has been issued, by which entity, and for which system version?
Which harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, and where an alternative solution was adopted, how is equivalence justified?
When does the certificate expire and which events force re-assessment before that date?

data_elements.name: Conformity assessment route
data_elements.description: Procedure used to demonstrate conformity.

data_elements.name: Notified body identifier
data_elements.description: Identification number of the body that issued the certificate.

data_elements.name: Certificate reference
data_elements.description: Certificate type, number and issuing body.

data_elements.name: Certificate expiry date
data_elements.description: Date on which the certificate ceases to be valid.

data_elements.name: Standard applied
data_elements.description: Harmonised standard or specification applied, with version.

artifacts.name: Declaration of conformity
artifacts.description: Signed declaration by the provider that a specified system version meets the applicable requirements, with the standards applied and any certificate references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Declaration identifier issued by the provider, bound to system master identifier and covered system version.

findings.name: Public registration record
findings.description: The public database entry representing the system, the split of registration duties between provider and deployer, which fields are publicly visible and how currency of the entry is maintained.

questions.text: Which public database entry represents this system, and what is its resolvable identifier or URL?
Which registration fields must be supplied and kept up to date by the provider, and which by the deployer?
Which registration data are publicly visible and which are restricted to authorities?
When was the registration entry created and last updated, and what triggers a mandatory update?

data_elements.name: Registration entry URL
data_elements.description: Resolvable location of the public registration entry for the system.

data_elements.name: Registration section
data_elements.description: Which registration section applies: provider high-risk, provider non-high-risk determination, or deployer.

data_elements.name: Registered status
data_elements.description: Status recorded in the public entry: on the market, in service, no longer available, recalled.

data_elements.name: Registration last-updated time
data_elements.description: Time at which the registration entry was last updated.

artifacts.name: Registration submission record
artifacts.description: Record of what was submitted to the public database, by whom, when, and which version of the entry it produced.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Registration entry identifier issued by the operating authority as the governed external identifier; the system master identifier remains the internal key.

layers.name: Transparency and Disclosure
layers.description: What affected people are told and how machine-generated output is marked.

findings.name: Disclosure to affected persons and content marking
findings.description: How natural persons are informed that they interact with an AI system or are subject to its decisions, how synthetic audio, image, video and text output is marked in a machine-readable and detectable form, which exemptions are relied on and how disclosure meets accessibility requirements.

questions.text: How and at what moment are natural persons informed that they are interacting with an AI system?
How is synthetic output marked in a machine-readable format that is detectable as artificially generated or manipulated?
Which disclosure exemptions are relied on for this system, and what safeguards replace disclosure?
How is the disclosure made accessible to persons with disabilities and to persons subject to automated decisions?

data_elements.name: Disclosure mechanism
data_elements.description: Means by which AI interaction or AI-assisted decision-making is disclosed.

data_elements.name: Disclosure timing
data_elements.description: Point relative to first interaction or exposure at which disclosure occurs.

data_elements.name: Content marking method
data_elements.description: Machine-readable marking technique applied to synthetic outputs.

data_elements.name: Disclosure exemption
data_elements.description: Recorded basis for not disclosing, with compensating safeguards.

artifacts.name: Transparency notice
artifacts.description: The user-facing notice content and its delivery configuration, together with the marking configuration applied to generated outputs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus notice revision plus locale; marking configuration is versioned with the baseline.

layers.name: Risk Management and Impact Assessment
layers.description: The continuous risk process and the assessment of effects on persons and their rights.

findings.name: Risk management system
findings.description: The continuous iterative risk process maintained across the system lifetime: identification and characterisation of risks by probability and severity of harm, the treatment measures adopted, the residual risks accepted and by whom, and the review cadence and out-of-cycle triggers.

questions.text: How is the risk management system established, documented and maintained as a continuous iterative process across the lifetime of the system?
How is each identified risk characterised in terms of probability of occurrence and severity of harm?
Which residual risks are accepted, by which role, and on what documented grounds?
What cadence governs risk review, and which events force an out-of-cycle reassessment?

data_elements.name: Risk entry
data_elements.description: One identified risk with source, affected parties and treatment status.

data_elements.name: Risk severity
data_elements.description: Rated severity of harm for a risk entry.

data_elements.name: Risk probability
data_elements.description: Rated probability of occurrence for a risk entry.

data_elements.name: Risk treatment measure
data_elements.description: Measure adopted to eliminate or reduce a risk.

data_elements.name: Residual risk acceptance
data_elements.description: Recorded acceptance of a residual risk with accepting role and time.

artifacts.name: Risk management file
artifacts.description: Living file describing the risk management system, the risk register for the system, treatment measures and residual risk acceptances.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus file revision; entries carry their own risk identifiers and revision history.

findings.name: Impact assessment on persons and rights
findings.description: Whether an impact assessment on fundamental rights is required for a given deployment, what it covers, how it relates to the data protection impact assessment, which groups are affected and how the findings summary reaches the authority.

questions.text: Is an impact assessment on fundamental rights required for this deployment, and what must it cover?
answer_data: Due timing relative to first use

questions.text: How does the AI impact assessment relate to and reuse the data protection impact assessment for the same processing?
Which categories of persons or groups are likely to be affected, and how were they or their representatives consulted?
What summary of findings is submitted to the competent authority, and where is the full assessment retained?

data_elements.name: Impact assessment scope
data_elements.description: Processes, purposes, frequency and affected persons covered by the assessment.

data_elements.name: Affected group
data_elements.description: Category of persons likely to be affected by use of the system.

data_elements.name: Data protection impact assessment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the DPIA covering the same processing.

data_elements.name: Impact assessment summary reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the summary of findings submitted upon registration.

artifacts.name: Impact assessment report
artifacts.description: Assessment of the effect of a specific deployment on persons and their fundamental rights, with the summary of findings prepared for the authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Deployer entity identifier plus system master identifier plus assessment revision; the submitted summary references the full report revision.

bundles.name: Post-market, Incidents and Retirement
bundles.description: How the system is watched after release, what happens when it harms, and how it ends.
bundles.rationale: Post-market monitoring, awareness-triggered incident reporting and log retention are explicit continuing obligations that outlive the release event and must be modelled as ongoing state, not one-off documents.

layers.name: Post-market Monitoring and Incidents
layers.description: The monitoring plan and signal set, and the detection and reporting of serious incidents.

findings.name: Post-market monitoring plan and signals
findings.description: The proportionate monitoring system that actively collects and analyses performance data over the lifetime of the system, including data supplied by deployers, the thresholds that trigger investigation, and the integration with pre-existing sectoral post-market systems.

questions.text: What does the post-market monitoring plan require to be collected, analysed and reviewed over the system's lifetime?
Which data do deployers supply to the provider, through which channel and at what frequency?
Which thresholds in monitored data trigger investigation or corrective action?
How is monitoring integrated with pre-existing sectoral post-market systems without duplicating obligations?

data_elements.name: Post-market monitoring plan reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the monitoring plan forming part of the technical documentation.

data_elements.name: Monitored signal
data_elements.description: A signal collected and analysed in post-market monitoring.

data_elements.name: Deployer feedback channel
data_elements.description: Channel through which deployers supply monitoring data to the provider.

data_elements.name: Monitoring threshold
data_elements.description: Threshold on a monitored signal that triggers investigation or corrective action.

artifacts.name: Post-market monitoring plan
artifacts.description: Plan describing systematic collection, documentation and analysis of performance data over the lifetime of the system, forming part of the technical documentation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus plan revision; plan revisions are bound to the technical documentation version they accompany.

findings.name: Serious incident detection and reporting
findings.description: What counts as a serious incident for this system, how awareness is established and timestamped, which reporting deadline class applies, which authority receives the report, and what investigation and corrective action follow.

questions.text: What qualifies as a serious incident for this system, and by which detection route is it recognised?
By which deadline must the incident be reported after awareness, and which deadline class applies?
To which market surveillance authority is the report addressed, and who signs it on behalf of which operator?
What investigation, risk assessment and corrective action follow the report, and how is the outcome recorded?

data_elements.name: Incident case identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of an incident case affecting this system.

data_elements.name: Incident deadline class
data_elements.description: Which reporting deadline class applies: general, accelerated for widespread infringement or critical infrastructure disruption, or death.

data_elements.name: Awareness timestamp
data_elements.description: Time at which the reporting operator became aware of the incident, which starts the deadline clock.

data_elements.name: Reporting authority
data_elements.description: Market surveillance authority to which the report is submitted.

data_elements.name: Corrective action reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the corrective action taken following an incident.

artifacts.name: Serious incident report submission
artifacts.description: Record of the submission of an incident report naming this system, with awareness time, deadline class, authority and acknowledgement; the report narrative itself is owned by the incident model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Incident case identifier issued by the reporting operator's system of record, cross-referenced to the authority's acknowledgement reference where one is issued.

layers.name: Retention, Decommissioning and Deletion
layers.description: How long records are kept, how the system is withdrawn and how personal data is disposed of without destroying auditability.

findings.name: Record retention and decommissioning
findings.description: Retention periods and legal bases for logs, technical documentation and evaluation evidence; the withdrawal, recall and decommissioning procedure including deployer notification and data disposition; and the terminal status record that keeps a withdrawn system discoverable.

questions.text: How long are logs, technical documentation and evaluation evidence retained, and under which legal or contractual basis?
What steps decommission the system, including withdrawal from market, deployer notification and disposition of data and models?
How are personal data in logs, caches and derived stores deleted or minimised while preserving audit capability?
What terminal status is recorded for a withdrawn system, and where does that record remain discoverable?

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which a class of record is retained, with the minimum where one is prescribed.

data_elements.name: Retention basis
data_elements.description: Legal, regulatory or contractual basis for the retention period.

data_elements.name: Decommissioning plan reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the plan governing withdrawal and decommissioning.

data_elements.name: Deletion record
data_elements.description: Evidence that data disposition was executed for a store.

data_elements.name: Terminal status
data_elements.description: Final recorded status of the system after withdrawal or recall.

artifacts.name: Decommissioning and retention record
artifacts.description: Record of retention schedules per record class and of the executed decommissioning steps, notifications, deletions and terminal status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System master identifier plus decommissioning event sequence; the record survives the system it describes for the length of the longest retention period.

functions.name: Register AI system
functions.description: Create the governed record for an AI system, assign its master identifier and bind provider, trade name, identification reference and intended purpose.
preconditions: Provider role is assigned to a legal entity
Intended purpose is declared in writing
effects: A uniquely identified AI system record exists
Downstream artifacts can reference a stable system key

functions.name: Classify risk and regulatory status
functions.description: Determine the applicable regime and record the classification route, any derogation condition, the profiling flag and the assessment evidence.
preconditions: Intended purpose is fixed
Deployment jurisdictions are known
effects: Obligation set for the system is determined
Registration and documentation duties are triggered or excluded

functions.name: Assemble component inventory
functions.description: Produce a machine-readable bill of materials for a baseline covering models, libraries, services, hardware, datasets and their suppliers, licences and vulnerabilities.
preconditions: A configuration baseline has been declared
BOM specification version is selected
effects: Supply-chain composition is inspectable by machine
Change detection on components becomes possible

functions.name: Baseline configuration
functions.description: Freeze and attest a configuration baseline, recording component versions, integrity digests and effective dates, and superseding the prior baseline.
preconditions: All components resolve to fixed versions
Release gate criteria have passed
effects: The operative system version is unambiguous
Later evidence can be bound to a specific baseline

functions.name: Evaluate and record performance
functions.description: Execute validation and testing against declared metrics and acceptance criteria and retain dated, signed evaluation evidence.
preconditions: Metrics are defined and justified as appropriate
Evaluation data are separated from training data
effects: Declared accuracy is substantiated
Release decisions have documented evidence

functions.name: Emit and retain operational logs
functions.description: Record events automatically over the system lifetime with distinct event and record times, protect their integrity and retain them for the prescribed minimum period.
preconditions: Logging capability is enabled in the baseline
Clock source and offset handling are defined
effects: Traceability of operation is preserved
Post-market analysis and incident reconstruction are possible

functions.name: Assess and authorise change
functions.description: Classify a proposed change as routine, pre-authorised or substantial, run the required impact assessment and tests, and authorise or refuse the new baseline.
preconditions: Current baseline is identified
Acceptance criteria are defined
effects: Conformity status after change is determined
Re-assessment and re-registration duties are triggered where needed

functions.name: Publish registration record
functions.description: Submit and maintain the public registration entry for the system, splitting provider and deployer fields and keeping status and instructions current.
preconditions: Classification determines a registration duty
Conformity evidence exists for the version being registered
effects: The system is publicly discoverable to authorities and, where applicable, the public
Status changes become externally visible

functions.name: Detect and report serious incident
functions.description: Recognise a serious incident, timestamp awareness, select the applicable deadline class, submit the report to the competent authority and drive investigation and corrective action.
preconditions: Incident categories are defined for the system
Reporting authority is identified for the jurisdiction
effects: Statutory reporting deadlines are met or a deviation is recorded
An incident report record is created and linked to this system

functions.name: Withdraw and decommission system
functions.description: Withdraw or recall the system, notify deployers and authorities, execute data disposition under the retention schedule and record the terminal status.
preconditions: Authorisation to withdraw exists
Retention obligations are identified per record class
effects: The system stops being placed on the market or put into service
Auditability is preserved for the required retention period

functions.name: Authorise placing on the market or putting into service
functions.description: Confirm technical documentation, human oversight, verification and validation, and conformity evidence before first making available or first use.
preconditions: Risk class and intended purpose are current; prohibited uses are blocked
effects: Placing-on-market or putting-into-service event time is recorded; the system may be used under its envelope

functions.name: Operate with human oversight
functions.description: Run the system inside its operating envelope with designated human interpretation, override and halt paths.
preconditions: Authorised deployer and overseers are in place; access policy permits operation
effects: Outputs are produced under logged oversight; out-of-envelope use is an exception

functions.name: Assess risk and impact
functions.description: Identify harms, treat risks, and perform or update AI system impact assessments and fundamental-rights assessments as required.
preconditions: Intended purpose and affected persons are identified
effects: Residual risk and mitigations are recorded against risk tolerance

functions.name: Monitor post-market performance
functions.description: Collect experience of use, measure drift and accuracy, and identify corrective or preventive actions, including linkage to incident reports.
preconditions: A post-market monitoring plan exists for systems that require one
effects: Performance evidence is updated; serious incidents can be referenced without absorbing the incident file

functions.name: Produce and disclose conformity evidence
functions.description: Assemble technical documentation, instructions, logs, declarations and registration data for deployers, competent authorities or the EU database.
preconditions: Identity, class and documentation revision are current
effects: An inspectable evidence package exists with integrity protection

composition.purpose: AI System specialises the software-product parent with inference-derived behaviour, autonomy and adaptiveness; non-AI packaging, release and functional semantics stay in the parent.

An AI system uses one or more model artifacts; this model holds the binding (version, role, access mode, upstream provider) and delegates parameters, training provenance and model-level evaluation to the artifact model.
An AI system may expose agent actors; this model records their existence, autonomy envelope and containment controls while agent goals, tools and delegation semantics live in the agent model.
An AI incident report names affected AI systems; this model holds detection, awareness time, deadline class and submission linkage, not the report narrative or authority correspondence.
Provider, deployer, importer, distributor and authorised representative are legal entities resolved by reference; this model stores role assignment and effective period only.
Evaluation datasets and operational input sources are referenced by identifier and version; dataset content, collection and labelling remain in the dataset model.

Baseline generation, change authorisation, evaluation runs and state transitions are expressed as Entity/Activity/Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, startedAtTime and endedAtTime.
Findings are mapped to the nine Annex IV documentation points as an alignment; no conformance is claimed and mapping gaps are recorded rather than asserted as satisfied.
Registration data elements are aligned to Sections A, B and C so a projection can populate a public entry without redefining the fields locally.
Trustworthiness characteristics and the GOVERN/MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE functions are used as an evaluation and governance vocabulary; the framework is voluntary and creates no conformance obligation.

composition.target: NIST AI 100-2 E2025 adversarial ML taxonomy
composition.purpose: The threat-class mapping data element draws its controlled vocabulary from the evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse taxonomy and its lifecycle stages of attack.

composition.target: ECMA-424 CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification
composition.purpose: The component inventory finding projects to a standard machine-readable BOM rather than defining a private inventory schema.
Organisation-level AI policy, impact assessment and supplier controls are supplied by the management system; this model consumes them by reference and does not restate management-system clauses.
Where the AI system is a device software function, the change-control finding extends to carry a pre-authorised Description of Modifications, Modification Protocol and Impact Assessment.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single accountable owner package for WM-AI-001 that holds the system-of-record for system master identifiers and resolves collisions between provider-internal and public registry identifiers.

The owner package must declare, per jurisdiction, which regulatory regime instance applies and which authority is the competent recipient for registration and incident reporting, because obligation sets are jurisdiction-bound.

The owner package must publish the controlled vocabularies it governs (risk class, autonomy level, adaptiveness mode, lifecycle stage, market status, threat class, deadline class) with versioning and deprecation rules.
